en: I can speculate about the past and express regret: must have been, can't have done, should have said.
I can build third and mixed conditionals: if plus past perfect, then would have, for a past that did not happen and its result today.
I can report information whose source is unclear with a passive structure: it is said that and he is thought to.
I can move the emphasis to the front with a cleft sentence: what I need is and it was … who.
I can use inversion after a negative adverbial at the front: rarely have I and not only did he.
I can join two sentences with a participle clause: having finished and being asked.
I can use non-defining relative clauses and relative pronouns after a preposition: …, which is why and the person to whom.
I can speak from a point in the future: the future perfect for what will be finished, the future continuous for what will be going on.
I can turn a verb into a noun for a formal register: the introduction of the rule instead of they introduced the rule.
I can soften a claim and steer the text: arguably, admittedly, to some extent, that said.
